title: Steering fleet-watcher alert
current: A steering session with an active seat and no live fleet watcher on its own machine receives a separate FLEET WATCHER ALERT hook block naming the exact re-arm command, with one --project per project where the session holds a live seat, read from its own cross-project `yoke claims steering list --session-id S --active-only`; a session with no seats is told so instead, and a failed seat read names its reason and that listing command. This holds in every mode (local universe and HTTPS) and on every harness. The client lists its own processes and applies the manifest wake model: a Monitor wait needs the wrapper plus a live yoke watch tail subscriber, notify_on_output needs the wrapper, and a harness without idle wake needs the in-turn wrapper, with scheduled re-entry only where Codex desktop tasks are available and the operator has not opted out. Keep one 15-minute task whose entire prompt/message is exactly `Keep steering`, without status, item lists, identifiers, cold-start instructions or handoff text. Normal steer entry recovers current project scope, facts and operator boundaries from the claimed strategy documents and their Live status; changing state stays there. Remove the task when steering ends, and never recreate it after an explicit stop until the operator asks to resume. Parked, ended or terminated sessions and unreadable process or posture reads get no alert. A Monitor subscription expires at its timeout_ms deadline (the manifest's idle_wake_subscription_limit_seconds); when only the tail lapsed while the wrapper runs, the alert names that same yoke watch tail capture and the deadline to arm it with, never a second wrapper. The watcher's wake stream carries only report rows new or changed apart from ages; the raw capture keeps every report whole. The byte ceiling drops the fleet report before the alert. The steer skill orders the start: seat held, handoff mail read, watcher attached, then the loop.
